title: Postgres in Docker
idea: Docker can run PostgreSQL for you. One command starts a container, an isolated process, from the `postgres:18` image, so you install nothing yourself.
points: An image is a packaged copy of the software; chapter 9 covers them.
The image requires `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. The user and database default to `postgres`.
`-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432` means IP, host port, container port; the IP keeps it local.
A named volume is Docker-managed storage; it keeps data when the container is removed.

hero.title: A database container and its volume

steps.caption: `docker run` pulls the `postgres:18` image if needed and starts a container named `bookstore-db`.
`-v` mounts a named volume. Postgres writes its data files into `bookstore-data`.
`-p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432` forwards port 5432 on your machine to the container. Your app connects to `localhost:5432`.
Your app runs a query. The tables and rows land in the volume.
`docker stop` stops the container. Nothing listens on the port, so connections fail.
`docker start` starts the same container again. The volume still holds your tables.
After `docker stop`, `docker rm` removes the container, not the named volume. A new `docker run` with the same `-v` finds the data.

code.title: Start and connect
code.caption: Needs Docker installed (chapter 9 covers it). Step through the flags; `demo-password` is a demo value.

walk.text: `docker run` starts a new container. `--name` gives it a name you can reuse.
`-e` sets an environment variable. `demo-password` is a demo value; choose your own.
`-v name:path` mounts a named volume, created if missing. This path is the one for Postgres 18.
`-p ip:host:container` publishes a port. `127.0.0.1` keeps it reachable from your machine only.
`-d` runs it in the background. The image, `postgres:18`, comes last.
`docker ps` lists running containers. Run `check.mjs` once Postgres is ready; `DATABASE_URL` is explained next lesson.
Stop and restart the container. The volume keeps your data.

code.title: Check the connection
code.caption: The script works the same against your container. The recorded run used a PostgreSQL 18 started for this book.

pitfalls: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only applies to an empty data directory; an old volume keeps its password.
Postgres 18 images recommend the mount `/var/lib/postgresql`; older guides use `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
Without `127.0.0.1`, `-p` publishes the port to all addresses, not just your machine.

quiz.q: Your container uses `-p 127.0.0.1:5433:5432`. Which port goes in `DATABASE_URL`?
quiz.why: After the IP, the host port comes first. Your app, outside Docker, connects to the host port.

takeaway: One `docker run` gives you Postgres; a named volume keeps its data.
